newsitem.title: INDIA: India drops all charges against Charles Sobhraj.
newsitem.headline: India drops all charges against Charles Sobhraj.

text.p: An Indian judge on Friday dropped all pending charges against renowned criminal Charles Sobhraj, paving the way for his deportation to France.
"I have no choice. If I had a choice I would stay here," Sobhraj, a French citizen, told reporters in the courtroom minutes before the acquittal order was passed by Judge Y.S. Jonwal.
The judge issued his acquittal order after Public Prosecutor B.L. Kalra said the government was dropping all charges relating to a dramatic 1986 jailbreak that earned Sobhraj fame.

"They'll put me on the first flight to Paris. I don't think I'll have any problems in France. I'm a French citizen," said Sobhraj, who has spent much of the past two decades in Indian prisons. "I'm attached emotionally to India. I feel part of India."

"It's only a matter of when the documents (court order) are handed over, and then he will have to leave India," said an official of India's Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO) who did not wish to be identified.

Minutes after the acquittal order, Sobhraj, wearing a sky-blue shirt and his trademark dark glasses and beret, was whisked away by FRRO officials in a blue police van. It was not immediately clear when he would be put on a plane out of the country.
